title: The permit
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: The county's derby permit comes in the mail. It's in the uncle's name. Gully fills in the form for him at the counter — rule four, broken, for the county. The uncle signs. His hand takes a long time.

panels.composition: The shack's counter. A county form, the letterhead as blocks. GULLY writing on it — on the counter. The UNCLE on his pot. WOOD.

image.prompt: a stocky teenager filling in an official form on a bait shack counter while an old man sits nearby and a young man watches, black and white, no words
image.notes: Rule four broken for the county; nobody mentions it.

panels.composition: Gully's hand writing. The blocks of the form. The signature line, empty.

image.prompt: close on a teenager's hand filling in an official form, the signature line still blank, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The uncle's hand signing. Slow. The pen pressing hard. The line wandering.

image.prompt: close on an old man's hand signing a form slowly, the pen pressing hard and the line wandering, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The form folded into an envelope. Gully licking it. The uncle looking at his own hand after. Wood drawing the hand, not the form.

image.prompt: an old man looking at his own hand after signing while a teenager seals an envelope and a young man draws, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: The uncle's signature takes a long time. Wood draws the hand.
